Listen to this article Share The defection of the vice chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State, five ward chairmen and other grassroots leaders to the All Progressives Congress (APC) could weaken the opposition party’s mobilisation capacity and reshape the political balance ahead of the 2027 general elections. Advertisement Advertisement The defectors, who also included ward secretaries, women and youth leaders and members of the Kwankwasiyya movement, announced their decision to join the APC on Monday during a visit to Abubakar Kabir Abubakar Bichi, member representing Bichi Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives. The delegation was led by Haladu Sa’adu, NDC vice chairman in Bichi, and included Mannir Umar, the party’s treasurer, as well as chairmen of Waire, Danzabuwa, Kaukau, Muntsira and Bichi wards. The development represents a significant loss of grassroots political structures for the NDC in the local government, particularly as political parties intensify mobilisation and alignments ahead of the next general elections. Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Abdulkadir Lawan, chairman of Danzabuwa Ward and the forum of ward chairmen, attributed their decision to what he described as Abubakar’s developmental interventions and commitment to improving the welfare of constituents. Lawan said his personal experience with the lawmaker’s educational support programme, which enabled him to pursue postgraduate studies, influenced his decision to join the APC. Advertisement He disclosed that he benefited from a scholarship programme facilitated through the Abubakar Kabir Foundation, which he said had also supported his ongoing PhD studies without intimidation or discrimination. According to him, the defectors were also dissatisfied with what they described as poor coordination and lack of respect for members within the NDC’s leadership structure in Kano State. Advertisement He cited internal party leadership issues, including concerns surrounding the leadership of Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, as additional factors behind their decision to leave the opposition party. Receiving the defectors, Abubakar welcomed their decision, describing their entry into the APC as an opportunity to strengthen the party’s grassroots organisation in Bichi. Advertisement Advertisement He urged them to contribute to party unity, mobilisation and effective coordination, while assuring them of their place in the party’s political structure. The lawmaker also highlighted some of his constituency interventions in Danzabuwa Ward, including the construction of a primary school, ongoing road projects and the provision of boreholes to improve residents’ access to potable water. He said sustained grassroots engagement and political unity would be necessary to secure electoral support for President Bola Tinubu, Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and other APC candidates in forthcoming elections. The defection comes amid political realignments in Kano State, where the strength of party structures at ward and local government levels is expected to play a significant role in determining electoral outcomes in 2027. The event was attended by Lawan Shehu Bichi, APC member representing Bichi Constituency in the Kano State House of Assembly; Sani Mukaddas Bichi, director-general of the campaign council; Babangida Danzabuwa, vice chairman of Bichi Local Government; Yusuf Muhammad Sabo, APC state secretary; and Ahmad Aruwa, special adviser on publicity. Other party stakeholders present included Bello Bawa Danzabuwa and Jamilu Kabir Bichi.
